_note: Phase 11.6 themed gardens. Pools list plant ids by role; 'tags' let other catalog plants fit the theme too (e.g. any plant that feeds butterflies). Plant lists are examples to verify (verified: false). Users can mix themes.

themes.name: Butterfly & pollinator
themes.description: Host plants for caterpillars and nectar flowers for butterflies, bees and hummingbirds.
calendar_hints: Don't spray: caterpillars chewing milkweed and passionvine are the point.
Cut back tropical sage and porterweed in late winter.

themes.name: Salad garden
themes.description: Lettuce, greens, radishes and snack tomatoes. Florida's salad season is fall to spring.
calendar_hints: Plant greens every 2 to 3 weeks from October to February for a steady harvest.
Summer is too hot for lettuce here: try sweet potatoes or okra instead.

themes.name: Herb garden
themes.description: Kitchen herbs by the door. Mint always goes in a pot.
calendar_hints: Cilantro and parsley grow in the cool months; basil and Cuban oregano love summer.

themes.name: Fruit garden
themes.description: Low-chill fruit that actually fruits in Florida, picked for your zone.
calendar_hints: Plant fruit trees in winter (December to February) so roots grow before summer heat.
Buy citrus only from a registered nursery (citrus greening).

themes.name: Rose & cut flower
themes.description: Florida-tough roses plus easy cut flowers for the vase.
calendar_hints: Prune roses lightly in late January and again in late August.
Water roses at the base in the morning to limit black spot.

themes.name: Salsa & pizza garden
themes.description: Tomatoes, peppers, onions and herbs for family cooking nights.
calendar_hints: Plant tomatoes and peppers in late winter (Feb to Mar) or late summer (Aug to Sep) in central Florida.

themes.name: Shade garden
themes.description: Ferns, coontie, bromeliads and caladiums for north-facing or tree-covered yards.
calendar_hints: Shade beds need less water: check the soil before you water.

themes.name: Low-maintenance (Florida-Friendly)
themes.description: The least water and care: natives and tough non-invasives that fit your yard.
calendar_hints: Mulch 2 to 3 inches deep once a year and you're mostly done.

themes.name: Kids' garden
themes.description: Fast, fun and easy: sunflowers, snack tomatoes, strawberries and beans.
calendar_hints: Radishes and beans are ready in weeks: great for short attention spans.

themes.name: Tropical
themes.description: Big leaves and bold color: hibiscus, bananas, bromeliads and firebush.
calendar_hints: Cover tropicals on the few cold nights below 35°F.

themes.name: Balcony & containers
themes.description: Pots for a balcony or patio: herbs, cherry tomatoes and a pollinator pot.
calendar_hints: Pots dry out fast: on hot west balconies check them every morning in summer.
